description:
defk-6tt (merged 2026-10-10) recovered dot, cosine and scale to within noise of the unchecked loop by accumulating a branchless non-finite flag per flat strip and replaying the strip on failure. It covers a strip only when, with the float checks taken out, no other check remains in the body (no bounds check, no i64 overflow check, no input write). Rolling mean_std (examples/rolling_stats.exs) fails that test: its strip has index arithmetic with overflow checks and array reads with bounds checks that can be elided only partly, so it keeps the per-operation float checks and stays at about +30% (bench/float_checks.exs). The author tried testing the flag before each remaining check (so the first error in program order still wins) and measured +41%, so it was taken out. Loops that can exit early through reduce_while (`:exits`) are also excluded.

Two directions, measure both: (1) widen the strip condition: when the remaining checks are only bounds checks that range facts could elide (defk-upc widens those facts) the strip becomes flaggable for free; the mean_std kernel's `x[i - w]` read with `i >= w` from an `if` is exactly a fact the compiler does not carry yet (conditional facts from the guarding `if`); (2) make every check in a strip branchless: bounds and overflow checks also OR into flags (`__builtin_add_overflow` already yields a flag; the bounds check is a compare), with one replay for any failure, which keeps program order because the replay runs the fully checked body from the strip start; the cost is a few more ORs per element, not a branch. (2) is general; (1) is the cheap win for this kernel.

Done when: mean_std measures within 10% of unchecked in bench/float_checks.exs, the non-finite raise-order tests and the resume tests still pass, and the README numbers are updated.

comments.text:
Measured provisionally UNDER LOAD (other agents building/testing, load avg 5-7.5), branch 5dbf94e (+ merge 0d5c424). bench/float_checks.exs, 1M elements, 3 runs x 11 interleaved rounds, best of 5 per round, main measured in the same session between runs:
- mean_std cost: run medians +8.2%, +7.1%, +8.5% (min/min 8.2%, 9.7%, 8.6%; single rounds 2.9..11.9%). Main same session: 38.2%, 37.1%, 39.2%. Within 10% on medians, not in every round.
- mean_std absolute: checks on 1937-1956 us (main 2621-2637), checks off 1788-1816 us (main 1893-1899).
- dot/cosine: run medians -1.8..0.9% (noise). scale (unchanged C): 7.7-14.8% this session, main measured 4.3-14.9% in the same session -> noise under load.
Direction 2 (joined branchless flags) alone did NOT pay for mean_std: on main-equivalent sqrt it measured +15% slower checks-on and +11-14% slower checks-off than main's predicted branches (loop is scalar, nothing to vectorise); with __builtin_sqrt +6-8% on, ~0 off. What pays is what flagging allows: seen_later/1 leaves out checks whose inf/NaN always reaches a later checked float expression (the two [f64] reads feeding the sticky window sums, and mean feeding the variance expression), sqrt(max(x, 0.0)) needs no check, and sqrt is __builtin_sqrt. Hand-edited C experiments (same session): flagged body with those three checks removed = +7-8% vs +32-42% with them. Direction 1 (conditional facts from the guarding if) not implemented: x[i - w] would also need w >= 0, which nothing in the kernel proves (w <= 0 always raises in Elixir mode too), and i - w / w - 1 / m + i - w + 1 overflow checks stay; so for this kernel (1) cannot make the strip check-free. Follow-up filed. Other catalog loops: only Examples.Kernels.mean_var newly flagged (min 3495-3502 us vs main 3452-3477, ~+1%, noise level); FuzzySearch search loops no longer flagged (defk-60q), min +1-2%/median +-1% (noise).

title: Strips with mixed checks (bounds, overflow, float) keep per-operation float checks: rolling mean_std still +30%
